title: Amazon S3 Basics
description: Learn about S3 buckets, objects, storage classes, versioning, encryption, bucket policies, and ACLs.

data.text: Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is an object storage service built to store and retrieve any amount of data from anywhere on the web. S3 stores data as objects in buckets. A bucket is a container for objects, and each object is a file and its metadata. S3 is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) of durability.

data.title: Object Storage vs Block Storage
data.text: S3 is object storage, which means data is stored as objects with metadata. This differs from block storage (like EBS), which stores data in fixed-size blocks. Object storage is ideal for unstructured data like images, videos, and backups.

Versioning keeps multiple versions of an object in the same bucket. If you overwrite or delete an object, the older version remains available. Encryption protects your data at rest. S3 supports both server-side encryption (managed by S3 or your own KMS key) and client-side encryption (encrypted before upload).

Bucket policies are JSON documents attached to a bucket that define access permissions. Access Control Lists (ACLs) are an older mechanism for granting access to individual objects. AWS recommends using bucket policies and IAM identities instead of ACLs for most use cases.

terms.definition: A container for S3 objects. Bucket names must be globally unique.
A file stored in S3, consisting of data, metadata, and a key (filename).
A tier within S3 that determines cost, availability, and retrieval time.
A feature that keeps multiple versions of an object for recovery and history.
A JSON access policy attached to an S3 bucket to control who can access it.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: S3 stores objects in globally unique buckets
Multiple storage classes balance cost and access frequency
Versioning protects against accidental overwrites or deletions
Encryption protects data at rest using SSE or client-side methods
Bucket policies control access at the bucket level
